items.title: Dense-briefing hook warns but never blocks
items.why: dense-briefing-shapes fired 64 soft and 0 blocks this fortnight while the slug recurred 6 times in atone — advisory-only is measurably insufficient for this pattern.

proposal.change: Change exit code from 0 (advisory) to 1 (blocking) when the reply opens with a table, a bullet list, or a file path before any plain-sentence direct answer.

items.title: No gate for shipping unwalked surfaces
items.why: shipping-surface-without-utility-check recurred 4 times with no hook in the registered list matching this slug — text reminders have not moved it.

proposal.change: When a turn declares a UI page, surface, or rendered artifact done and the session has no chrome-devtools or playwright tool call against that surface this turn, block and require a screenshot or walk before the turn closes.

items.title: Unwalked-surface shipping rising 0→3 per week
items.why: shipping-surface-without-utility-check trajectory was 0, 0, 1, 3 over four consecutive weeks with no countervailing hook fire — a clean upward trend, not noise.

proposal.change: Prioritise this hook above other new hooks this week given the drift trajectory.

items.title: declared-ready gate misses softer readiness claims
items.why: declared-ready blocked 23 times and fired soft 41 times, yet the slug recurred 7 times — the blocked cases are terminal 'done' words; the soft cases include 'green on laptop', 'proven from the Pi API', 'passing on Mac' which the gate does not catch.

proposal.change: Expand trigger vocabulary to block 'proven from', 'confirmed on', 'green on', 'passing on' when followed by a single environment name (laptop, Mac, Pi, staging) and no tool-call artifact returning that environment's output exists in the same turn.

items.title: guard-lazy-question nudges but never blocks
items.why: guard-lazy-question fired 6 nudge and 0 blocks; asked-owner-for-a-value-already-derivable recurred 3 times including a literal '?' placeholder committed into a spec.

proposal.change: Promote from nudge to block when the question names a URL, filename, branch name, or pairing value that a command in the session allow-list would deterministically supply.

items.title: PR title flags missing across repos
items.why: pr-title-missing-required-flag recurred 3 times across independent sessions and repos; guard-github-agent-marker checks attribution lines but not the [noslack]/[nobot] title tokens or Linear ticket references that keep being omitted.

proposal.change: Before allowing gh pr create, verify the --title value contains [noslack] and at least one Linear ticket token matching [A-Z]+-[0-9]+; block and print the missing tokens if either check fails.

items.title: Truncated skill listing causes false absence claims
items.why: Two independent sessions record corrections where the agent denied a skill existed because the session skill listing was truncated; guard-absence-claim targets code symbols, not skill names.

proposal.change: When the turn contains 'X is not installed' or 'X does not exist' and X matches the hyphenated-lowercase skill naming convention, block and require a grep of ~/.claude/skills/ before the claim is allowed to stand.

items.title: AI-smell prose persists past prose-smell gate
items.why: prose-smell blocks 6 times and nudges 335, yet ai-smell-prose-against-stored-voice recurred 7 times from 2 sources — the gate catches em-dashes but misses audit-register PR body structure and euphemism patterns in RCAs.

proposal.change: Add a PR-body path: when the Bash call is gh pr create, scan --body for Verdict/Boundary/not-verified-by-hand patterns and block unless the /pr-description skill was invoked this turn.

items.title: Status-report turns concentrate word-salad events
items.why: Session 65da91a2 produced 8 atone events in one session — dense table for a one-sentence question, twelve manual commands instead of one script, and an unasked core-dump — all in turns responding to owner status or handoff requests.

proposal.change: Add a second trigger: when the user message is a status question ('what is gated on me', 'what waits on me') or follows a /catchup invocation and the reply body exceeds 4 lines before the first actionable sentence, block.

items.title: Memory-sourced URLs and CI status cited as live facts
items.why: Three events record the agent citing a URL from memory (ScraperAPI dashboard), a CI status from a plan doc rather than a runner log, and a wrong workflow filename — all share the pattern of treating stored context as current state without a command-derived citation.

proposal.change: Extend the URL pattern: when a reply names an external dashboard or CI run URL and no tool call this turn returned that URL in its output, fire a block requiring the URL to be derived from a command rather than cited from memory.

items.title: Slack-automation session cluster is covered elsewhere
items.why: The two structural mistakes (skill absence claim, model-id check) are already surfaced by c-e21c31ba and the model-tier hook; the remaining corrections (command guard on quoted arguments, pending items) do not form an independent pattern.

items.title: e2e workflow filename is a one-off path error
items.why: The two atone events cite the same filename error in the same session, and the affirm event is unrelated; this is a single incident surfaced by path-hotspot scoring, not a recurring pattern.

items.title: abbc0880 is a sub-case of dense-briefing
items.why: Cluster has two correction signals and one proposal about goal concreteness; the proposal (prop-20261009-144110-4c) is a text injection and the pattern merges into c-ab3c677c.

named.process_note: The 2026w41 amendment requested exit-1 vs exit-0 counts per hook. The current data separates block from soft/nudge, which partially satisfies this, but 'soft' conflates exit-0-advisory with exit-0-muted-by-file. Adding a third column (muted) would let the reader distinguish a hook whose logic is wrong (fires exit-0 when it should exit-1) from one the owner deliberately muted — this would have resolved c-0d4db80b's 'declared-ready blocks 23 but pattern persists 7' question directly, because it would show how many of the 41 soft fires were muted vs genuinely advisory.
